title: Chicken With 40 Garlics
ingredients: 6 sprigs fresh thyme, or ½ tsp, dried
2 cups white wine/chicken stock (50/50 or your choice, maybe with a dash of cognac)
directions: Chicken with 40 Cloves of Garlic is a classic French recipe. The garlic mellows in flavor as it cooks and you end up with mild, buttery cloves paired with a moist and delicious chicken.

If you don’t have ready access to grocery-store bags or bottles of peeled whole garlics: Add 2 cups of water to a saucepan and bring to a boil. Separate garlic cloves (you don’t need to peel them) and add to the water. Cook for 1 minute, then drain and peel garlic.
Pat the chicken pieces dry with paper towels and season well with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat a large deep pan or skillet over medium heat. Add 2 Tablespoons butter and oil until hot.

Add chicken, skin side down (cook in batches if you can’t fit all of the thighs at once) and cook for 5 minutes, until the skin is golden brown. Flip and cook on the other side for 3 minutes. Take the chicken out for a minute or two.

Add the garlic, wine, and chicken stock (dash of nutmeg and/or cognac optional), scrapping up any bits in the pan. Snuggle the chicken back into the pan (skin-side up) and add the thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer. (Maybe add some little peeled carrots if you want a vegetable here.)
Cover the skillet and cook over med-low heat for 30-35 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through. You could also bake this in a 350 degree over for about the same amount of time.
Transfer the chicken and garlic (carrots?) to a platter and cover with foil to keep warm. Discard the bay leaf and thyme sprigs.

Turn the skillet to higher heat and cook until the liquid has reduced a little bit, about 3-5 minutes. Whisk the cornstarch into some of the stock in a side dish, then add it to the pot and cook until the sauce has slightly thickened, 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in remaining 2 Tablespoons of butter. Place the chicken on a serving platter and pour sauce over the chicken.
Serve with buttered noodles or mashed potatoes to absorb the wonderful sauce. Be sure to have some tasty baguette or French bread for spreading the cooked garlic cloves on.
